SMTO-TSK-0064 — You can't delete this task because others wait on it

GUID: 98cd67e1-297b-4ef5-9caf-fde90d791971
Slug: task-dependency-history-required
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • Another task in this conversation was set to run after this one, so SMTO keeps this task's history to show why. Nothing was deleted.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Leave this task in place if you still need the conversation; it does no harm there. Other tasks rely on its history to explain the order they ran in.
  2. If you don't need any of this conversation, first let any running task finish or select Stop on it. SMTO won't remove a conversation while work in it is still active.
  3. Then delete the whole conversation from the conversation list using Delete conversation. Removing the whole conversation removes this task and the tasks that wait on it together.

What success looks like

  • The task stays in the conversation, or the whole conversation disappears from your conversation list after you delete it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't try to remove the waiting order by hand; the task history is kept on purpose.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Task deletion was refused (DEPENDENCY_REFERENCED) because another retained task's dependency edge references the selected task.

What this means

  • Task deletion finds another retained task's dependency edge referencing the selected task. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • Task deletion finds another retained task's dependency edge referencing the selected task.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect dependent task references, including completed/cancelled history, before attempting deletion.

How to fix it

  • Referenced task history is kept until the whole conversation is removed. Keep the task, or delete the conversation once all its active work has finished; do not retry the single-task delete with a stale identifier.
  • Keep the referenced history, or use the supported whole-conversation removal flow after active work is settled.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • History remains available until a supported scope-wide removal safely accounts for all dependent work.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
